A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSA/RAMba research despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, retrieval, downstream-task and efficiency experiments in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a stick-breaking ablation and 2.7B-scale model results.

M1.justification: The core hierarchical attention, stick-breaking aggregation and shared-cache architecture remain. Appendix E adds a pretrained-model adaptation procedure using frozen-backbone copying warmup followed by LoRA/HSA training. Section 3.1 also adds square-root dimension scaling to the written chunk-score formula, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1 introduces repeated-sentence copying as a training task for the larger model. Evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged; v2's 'Code' uses the same dataset citation as v1's CodeParrot. Increasing model size alone does not expand dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The original Transformer, Mamba-2, SWA and NSA comparisons are retained. The larger-model experiment uses the existing Mamba-2 comparator family. Flash-Attn is identified more explicitly as FlashAttention-2 with unchanged plotted results; newly cited MiniCPM4 is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The retained 370M experiments keep their settings, while Appendix E introduces substantial new protocols for 2.7B-scale models: 32K-context post-training stages and a separate RULER route with 60B pretraining tokens and 1B synthetic fine-tuning tokens. Table 5's claim that these models were trained on 4K contexts conflicts with the 32K LongBench training recipe.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds a controlled comparison replacing stick-breaking weights with positional-encoding-free softmax in RAMba without memory reset. This tests the weighting mechanism directly. Existing encoder, memory-reset, offloading and sharing analyses remain.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly discloses one checkpoint per pretrained model and explains the absence of error bars. It asserts that multiple datasets and metrics support statistical significance, but adds no confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run estimates. One checkpoint does not establish a training-run count.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and efficiency values are retained. New Table 5 reports larger-model results, including RAMba's 27.3 LongBench overall score and 100.00 Variable Tracking score at 64K. The added Table 1 ablation reports 64K ArXiv perplexity of 6.05 versus the retained 3.87 with stick-breaking. These substantially extend the evidence without demonstrating same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: New Appendix A formalizes chunk relevance as summed normalized attention mass, contrasts it with mean-logit selection, and supplies a numerical ranking counterexample in Equations 1–3 and Figure 5. This adds mathematical reasoning beyond v1's conceptual explanation, but no general convergence theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about learned chunk retrieval, efficiency, length generalization and perfect 64M-context passkey retrieval after 4K pretraining remain. The introduction's revised extrapolation multiplier restates that existing result. The permanent-memory conclusion reframes an aspiration already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that empirical validation concentrates on Mamba and does not cover models above 3B parameters. Appendix A expands the explanation of selection errors and gradient feedback. The complex-task length-generalization caveat removed from the conclusion remains in Section 4.3.

D1.justification: Appendix E substantially expands architecture, freezing, LoRA, learning-rate, token-budget and compute-time documentation for the larger models. Appendix C newly reports approximately 60 hours on 16 PPUs for pretraining. A project repository link is added, although the checklist still describes code release as future. Existing 370M hyperparameters and relocated prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to LoRA, Retrieval-Pretrained Transformer, MiniCPM4 and CEPE, acknowledging architectural precedents and adaptation procedures while extending the conceptual sparse-attention comparison. The previous references and main related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, edits prose, clarifies grouped notation and rewrites the conclusion while retaining the main section structure and much of the wording. It expands appendix organization, moves the existing retrieval templates into Appendix D, and adds a limitations section and conference checklist.

P2.justification: Figures 5–8 add a substantial visual walkthrough of selection failure and hierarchical weighting, alongside the new larger-model Table 5 and expanded Table 1. Existing diagrams receive annotations and caption revisions, and performance plots receive label, typography or color changes while retaining their data.

improvement.justification: The targeted stick-breaking ablation, larger-model evidence and detailed adaptation recipe improve empirical support and reproducibility beyond v1. The gains are tempered by Table 5's 4K-versus-32K training inconsistency and the checklist's unsupported statistical-significance assertion. These reporting weaknesses limit the overall improvement despite the useful additions.
